Nilo, before Miami, let's do a quick debrief. What was the turning point for you in this block?
The negotiation lessons. If I hadn't practiced them, I would have felt nervous at the last board meeting.
I remember. You found a compromise on the renewal, and the vote was unanimous.
Yes. And now the agreement is binding, so the trade-off was worth it.
And the news lesson? Could you tell me what you learned there?
That an allegation is not a fact. I always check the source before I comment.

Hi Nilo, it's Daniel from the program group. I'm preparing the case study for our last session of the block, and I'd like your opinion. Here is the situation. A club and a sponsor were negotiating a renewal. The sponsor said that they wanted a longer contract, but the club asked for a higher fee. In the end, they found a compromise: three years, with a small increase. The board vote was unanimous. But there was a problem. Nobody checked one clause about image rights, and the contract was binding. If they had read that clause carefully, they would have avoided a big dispute. So my question for you is this: if you were the compliance officer of that club, what would you do now? Think about it, and we can discuss it on Thursday. Thanks!

Hello everyone, this is Sofia from the program office. Congratulations: you have now finished the second block of the program. Before the Miami module, each participant will have a short progress check with a tutor. It takes twenty minutes. First, the tutor will ask you about one turning point in your learning. Then you will summarize one case from the block, for example a negotiation or a news story. Finally, the tutor will ask you what you would do differently. Please bring one example of a real document from your work, like an email or a contract clause. If you cannot attend on your day, write to me, and I will find another time. Remember, this is not an exam. It is a conversation to help you prepare. See you soon.
